title: Tiered burn-window tuning and delayed paging to cut SLO alert noise
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Postmortem follow-up to recurring capacity/regression incidents: redesign burn-rate alert windows and introduce delayed-paging heuristics to reduce transient paging and align escalation with real customer impact. Focus on per-region thresholds, service-tier defaults, and a console visualization for burn-rate tuning.
actions: Lin Chen | 2026-03-18 | Implement configurable burn-rate windows: default 1m/5m/30m for S1, 30s/2m/15m for S2, expose in alert policy UI
Marco Ruiz | 2026-03-20 | Add delayed-paging toggle (N seconds) with adaptive backoff to suppress transient bursts; default 90s
Sofia Green | 2026-03-22 | Create new per-region SLO dashboard panels showing burn distribution and recent paged incidents
Aisha Patel | 2026-03-15 | Draft runbook updates and escalation mapping for tiered paging; replace immediate-page on first burn spike
Lin Chen | 2026-03-10 | Add deduplication rule by top-level service owner labels to reduce duplicate pages from infra and runtime alerts
Eng Oncall Rotation | 2026-03-25 | Run 2-week canary with new thresholds on non-prod region and collect false-positive rate
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Triage meeting — agreed to pursue window-tuning + delayed paging after examining three capacity incidents in Jan-Feb; prioritized as P1 for next cycle
2026-02-26: Prototype burn-window change in staging; saw 38% reduction in page events for transient 5–20s bursts without SLO misses
2026-03-03: Trade-off discussion — shorter windows reduce detection speed for real regressions; decision: keep multi-window approach and add delayed paging
2026-03-08: PR opened for alert-engine changes that add per-service config and dedupe labels (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/alerts/pull/478)
2026-03-11: UX mock for console control & visualization reviewed by PM and SRE; feedback: surface recommended defaults and historical false-positive rate
acceptance_criteria: Burn-rate paging frequency reduced by >=40% for non-customer-impacting bursts in canary regions
Paging latency for true-positive SLO breaches remains within current SLA targets
Console exposes per-service burn-window settings and shows historical FP/TP counts
Runbook updated and on-call rotation trained on new behavior
